groups.anti_collapse_protocol: MANDATORY and legible. (1) Each seat's post-zig-zag verdict table is persisted by the parent to research/artifact-placement-adjudication/returns/ and bound {path, sha256} before crosstalk opens. (2) Each seat MUST open its crosstalk contribution by restating its own final zig-zag verdict table VERBATIM, before reading or responding to any other seat. (3) Any post-exchange change to its own row is marked DRIFT with the seat that moved it and the argument that moved it; an unmarked change is a defect. (4) The reconciled table must carry, per row, which seats held which position pre-crosstalk, so a row of unanimity that was NOT unanimous before the exchange is visible as convergence rather than as independent agreement. (5) The residue list of unreconciled dissent may not be empty unless every seat's pre-crosstalk table already agreed on every row.

proposed_capability_profile.enforcement_note: effective_enforcement is non_observable: the write/spawn restrictions are a declared trust boundary on seat behaviour, not a runtime-checked gate. parent-only-writer is not independently verifiable from this profile alone, and no seat's compliance may be reported as enforced. The parent applies P8 (inspect the actual diff) before treating any seat claim as done.
proposed_capability_profile.rationale: every seat is an adjudicator, not a writer. The parent is the only writer and the final_approver; no seat may execute a move. The lineage seats additionally need blame/follow history, because plain git log over a path does not surface history across a rename and those seats' whole job is to test whether the record supports a lineage claim about moved artifacts.

capability_review.reviewer: read-only capability reviewer, proposal-gate helper exception (unregistered)
findings: under-grant on S-B / R-B / crosstalk: lineage seats were given git log/show/status but not git blame or git log --follow, so they could not test a lineage claim across a rename without either failing or silently exceeding the profile
enforceability gap: effective_enforcement is non_observable while the profile reads as if parent-only-writer were enforced
minor non-blocking over-grant: S-A/R-A/S-C/R-C receive git and hashing classes their angles never need

final_approver_obligations: P8: inspect the actual diff of every applied move before reporting it done; no seat claim is accepted as executed.

convergence check: before accepting the reconciled table, diff it against a mechanical merge of the three persisted post-zig-zag verdict tables. Any row that became unanimous only after crosstalk, and is not marked DRIFT with a named argument, is treated as suspected false consensus and is re-opened rather than applied.

cost-axis guardianship: neither R-D (executability) nor R-E (authority and residue) guards the COST pole of anti_bias_global downstream of crosstalk. The parent explicitly re-checks the reconciled table against S-C's final cost objections and records any that the table dropped without answering. This gap was named by check-tension round 2 helper 2 and is closed at the approver, not inside second-review, so that the second-review axis stays clean.
no seat may execute a move; the parent is the only writer.
